page.layout: One printed page with a single column of text. A narrow column of marginal notes stands at its right, beside the text lines. The left edge shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed. Below the text: the signature "B 4" and the catchword "aliter" at the right.

main_text.p: Deus; ut presente percussore, ipsum exangue cadaver, recentem sanguinem effundat: quod licet ad antipathiam alii, malim tamen ego, ut omnipotentem Dei digitam referre: ita Deo pariter & hominibus, Christianis & Barbaris, odiosum est, semperque fuit, vel ipsum homicidii nomen: res vero ipsa horroris plena. Concludamus itaque cum Regio Psalmista, {1} Libera me Domine, de sanguinibus, Deus, Deus salutis meae: eoque expectamus ardentius, quia (ut idem alibi:) {m} Viri sanguinum, & dolosi, non dimidiabunt dies suos: vel enim sibimet ipsis violentam mortem consciscunt, vel publico Magistratus gladio cadunt, vel in duello percunt, vel ipsius Dei digito feriuntur. Consulantur Historiæ, revolvantur Annales, & quotusquisque inveniatur homicida, cujus dies nō fuerint dimidiati[?]ita[?] ut intuens iratum Iudicem, expectans cruentum carnificem, sentiens mordentem conscientiam, metuens creaturas sanguinis vindices, in squalore viveret, & cum infamia moreretur. Stat enim, & in æternum stabit divini veritas oraculi, {n} Non1Psal.5.15.m Psal. 54. 27.n Num. 35. 31.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right: 1 Psal. 5.15.; m Psal. 54. 27.; n Num. 35. 31. The mark 1 is set small in the text. The word "dimidiatiita" is printed in a smudged state; the reading "dimidiati[?]ita" is doubtful, and the mark after it is also uncertain. The catchword "aliter" is italic, and the text ends with the italic "Non" at the mark n, so the phrase continues on the next page. Show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page on the left are not transcribed.
